page: Amazon Web Services c5d.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor operating at 3.4 GHz, this x86_64 instance provides two dedicated vCPUs mapped across a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled. The configuration includes 4.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, resulting in a compute-oriented 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. In addition to compute resources, the c5d.large includes a bundled 50 GB local NVMe SSD instance store volume alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Hardware accelerators such as discrete GPUs are not present.

Benchmark results demonstrate standard single-thread execution alongside limitations inherent to its single physical core topology. In synthetic processor evaluations, the c5d.large achieves average single-core throughput in stress-ng testing, but multi-core throughput is constrained due to thread contention over the single physical execution core. Memory bandwidth reaches 102.07 GB/sec for small cached blocks and stabilizes at 12.85 GB/sec for uncached reads. In application-focused metrics, the system delivers 2.06 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and handles 1.8 million Redis SET operations per second, supported by vector extensions including AVX-512F.

Resource allocation on the c5d.large provides a clear tradeoff favoring CPU clock frequency and local disk input-output speed over raw thread capacity or memory volume. Because local NVMe storage is directly attached, workloads avoid the latency and overhead of network-attached block volumes for scratch space. However, total memory is strictly limited to 4.0 GB, making the instance ill-suited for dense in-memory caches or heavily concurrent execution. The c5d.large is best matched with lightweight web serving, batch data transformation, continuous integration agents, and stateless processing tasks requiring fast temporary storage.
description: Amazon Web Services c5d.large is a compute-optimized instance utilizing the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8124M x86_64 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz. The instance delivers two dedicated vCPUs on one physical core with two threads per core, coupled with 4.0 GB of DDR4 system memory and 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. A distinctive hardware feature is its bundled 50 GB local NVMe SSD instance storage, enabling high-speed scratch disk capability without network block volume overhead. Benchmark evaluations show balanced single-core execution with moderate performance in stress-ng tests, though multi-threaded operations reflect the constraints of a single physical core. Memory bandwidth reaches 12.85 GB/sec on uncached reads, while Redis throughput hits 1.8 million operations per second. The c5d.large offers efficient dedicated compute and fast local IO for workloads such as web serving, continuous integration nodes, lightweight batch processing, and ephemeral caching.
